meta.title: Phosphor — Modern ANSI & ASCII Art Editor
meta.description: Turn images into ANSI or ASCII art in your browser, then paint, type, animate, and export.

app.noscript: Phosphor needs JavaScript enabled to run.

legal.desktopPrivacy: In a room, the people you connect with see your IP address. When you choose Check for Updates, it asks GitHub for Phosphor's releases, and GitHub sees your IP address. When you open Plugins, it asks phosphor.work for the plugin list, and phosphor.work sees your IP address. When you install a plugin from the Marketplace, it asks GitHub for the plugin's files, and GitHub sees your IP address. When you get a palette from Lospec by name or link, the app requests it from lospec.com, which sees the request and your IP address. When you press Send in Report an issue (in the Help menu), it sends what you wrote, your version of Phosphor and your system, and, if you left its box ticked, your drawing and the session's steps to Phosphor's server (api.phosphor.work, run on Cloudflare), which sees your IP address. What you wrote is published as an issue on GitHub. The drawing and the steps are kept for 90 days, and only Phosphor's developer sees them.

about.label: About Phosphor
about.tagline: Turn images into ANSI and ASCII art, then keep drawing with style.
about.p1: Phosphor began in 2019 as a small experiment to build tooling for a concept I called “ANSI Nouveau.” At the time, I was interested in the idea of recreating the mid-90s BBS experience I grew up with, but through a modern lens. Like many passion projects, life got in the way and it eventually landed on the shelf.
about.p2: A couple years later, I came across a fantastic {moebiusFork} that added 256-color and full-color support. It reminded me of this project, so I dragged it out of storage, dusted off the code, and leveraging modern tools and techniques, brought it back to life.
about.moebiusForkLink: fork of the Moebius ANSI editor
about.p3: While Phosphor started as an image-to-ANSI converter, today it brings the two workflows together. It turns images into ANSI or ASCII that you can fine-tune to your liking, then lets you draw and type over that cell by cell and export as .ans or .utf8ans. Finish your piece here, or take the file into another editor you love for a final pass. It supports going for that “Pure ANSI” or the full-color, UTF-8 “ANSI Nouveau” style that initially inspired the project.
about.p4: Phosphore is still evolving. Expect rough edges on phones and small tablets, though iPad with Apple Pencil works well in testing. Feedback, bug reports, and ideas are always welcome: open an issue on {github}, or fork the repo and take it in your own direction.

cols.label: Dimensions
cols.help: Canvas width in columns and height in pixel rows. Two pixel rows equal one character row. A typed size applies on Enter, Tab or a click elsewhere; Escape puts the field back.

renderStyle.help: ANSI mode sets colors for both the character and its background. Color ASCII draws colored characters on a black background, using denser shapes for stronger colors. Monochrome ASCII uses one color and maps brightness from light to dark.

chars.help: The characters used to convert images. ANSI chooses characters randomly, while ASCII maps them from dark to bright. Repeating a character makes it appear more often. Best match and By shape ignore repeated characters.

seed.help: Controls random character placement in ANSI mode. The same seed produces the same pattern. Generate a new seed to shuffle characters.

quantize.help: Full color preserves 24-bit color. VGA and CGA reduce colors to classic 256-color and 16-color palettes. Limited count picks the best colors from the image. Custom color list uses only the hex colors you enter.

ditherStyle.help: Chooses how colors blend together. Floyd–Steinberg scatters dots like film grain. Ordered creates a regular grid pattern that stays steady between animation frames.

dither.label: Dither
dither.help: Blends palette colors using fine dot patterns to create smooth gradients instead of harsh color bands. Direct painting does not dither. The base layer and each vector layer have their own dither setting. In Best match or By shape modes, characters also adapt to the dither pattern.

smoothing.help: Controls how the image resizes onto the grid. High blends smoothly. Low preserves sharp edges and pixel details.

colorizeStrength.label: Colorize
colorizeStrength.help: Tints the image toward a single color while preserving light and shadow.

hue.label: Hue shift
hue.help: Rotates colors around the color wheel.

invert.label: Invert
invert.help: Inverts all colors to their negatives. This applies after Colorize and Hue shift.

brightness.label: Brightness
brightness.help: Adjusts the overall image brightness lighter or darker.

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.help: Increases or decreases the difference between light and dark areas.

levelsBlack.label: Black point
levelsBlack.help: Sets the black point. Tones at or below this level become pure black, expanding the remaining tones.

levelsWhite.label: White point
levelsWhite.help: Sets the white point. Tones at or above this level become pure white, expanding the remaining tones.

levelsMid.label: Midtones
levelsMid.help: Adjusts midtone brightness. Values above 1 lighten midtones, and values below 1 darken them, without changing black or white.

saturation.label: Saturation
saturation.help: Adjusts color intensity from grayscale to vivid color.

posterize.label: Posterize
posterize.help: Reduces the number of colors in each channel to create flat, poster-like bands.

threshold.label: Threshold
threshold.help: Splits the image into two colors. Tones at or above this level use the light color, and darker tones use the dark color.

blur.label: Blur
blur.help: Softens noise and fine detail before converting the image. Applies to the base layer only; drawing layers are not affected.

flatten.label: Simplify
flatten.help: Groups similar colors together into clean, simplified shapes. Applies to the base layer only; drawing layers are not affected.

sharpen.label: Sharpen
sharpen.help: Sharpens edges and fine details. Applies to the base layer only; drawing layers are not affected.

edges.label: Edges
edges.help: Traces outlines using your chosen edge color. Applies to the base layer only; drawing layers are not affected.

edgeThickness.label: Edge thickness
edgeThickness.help: Controls the thickness of traced outlines. Applies to the base layer only; drawing layers are not affected.

charChoice.help: Random chooses characters using the seed value. Best match picks the character and colors that best match the image. By shape matches character outlines to image details in each cell.

charChoiceAscii.help: By intensity (Color ASCII) and By brightness (Monochrome ASCII) choose denser characters as cells get brighter. By shape matches character outlines to image details in each cell.

solids.label: Solids
solids.help: Controls how often solid color blocks are chosen instead of shaded blocks or half-blocks.

patternLight.label: Pattern light
patternLight.help: Controls how character foreground and background colors blend. At 0%, colors blend by simple average. At 100%, colors blend like light on a screen, making shaded cells appear brighter.

font.help: Sets the display font for your canvas. Load, save, and remove fonts (bitmap fonts, or monospaced TrueType, OpenType, or WOFF fonts from your computer) with Manage. Bitmap fonts look best at multiples of their native size (such as 16px or 32px for 8×16 fonts). Your font choice is saved in your browser. In a shared room, you see the host's font.

consent.title: Before you use Social rooms
consent.regionAria: Privacy and community information for Social rooms
consent.intro: Social mode lets you watch live drawing, draw with others, or host your own room. Here is how your privacy is protected.
consent.lobbyBody: Entering Social mode connects your browser to our server. People in the lobby can see your username (guests receive a random nickname). Public rooms show their host, title, viewer count, and a live preview.
consent.joiningBody: Your browser connects directly to the host's computer, so each of you can see the other's IP address, which may show your general city and internet provider. Use a VPN if you want to keep your IP address private. Chat messages are visible to everyone in the room.
consent.startingBody: People in your room see your drawing in real time and can see your IP address. Public rooms display a preview in the lobby. If you invite someone to draw, they receive a copy of the entire project, including the base image. If your room is reported, moderators receive a snapshot of the canvas to investigate.
consent.beKindBody: Do not harass, bully, or demean others. Do not misuse IP addresses or share private personal information. Keep public rooms appropriate, respect other artists' work, and submit reports in good faith only. Hosts can remove participants from their rooms. Signed-in users can block others, and those with a confirmed email can report rooms or users that violate our guidelines.

errors.solverFault: The solver “{name}” returned a character it doesn't draw with, so the first character of the set shows in its place.
errors.zipEncrypted: That .zip is password protected, which Phosphor can't open.
errors.zip64: That .zip uses the large-archive format, which Phosphor can't read.
errors.noManifest: There is no phosphor-plugin.json at the top of that, or one folder down.
errors.noScript: The plugin names a script, {path}, that isn't in it.
errors.tooBig: That file is too big for a plugin.
errors.notJson: That file isn't a plugin's manifest.
errors.newer: This plugin was made for a newer Phosphor.
errors.needsNewer: This plugin needs a newer Phosphor.
errors.nothing: This plugin adds nothing this Phosphor can use.
errors.badField: The manifest's “{field}” is missing or isn't right.
errors.unknownField: The manifest has a field this Phosphor doesn't know: “{field}”.
errors.unknownColor: The theme “{theme}” sets “{key}”, which isn't one of Phosphor's colors.
errors.badColor: The theme “{theme}” sets “{key}” to “{value}”, which isn't a hex color.
errors.otherPlugin: That file is now a different plugin ({id}).
errors.fileGone: That file can't be read anymore.
errors.notAllowed: The browser isn't letting Phosphor read that file.
errors.notKept: This browser didn't keep the plugin.
